translation_en: Surayj ibn Yunus and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us—the wording is Surayj's. They said: 'Abdullah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah gave us an additional award beyond our share of the fifth, and I received an old, large she-camel.

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us. Another chain: Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us. Both reported from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: I heard from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah gave a detachment an additional award, with the like of Ibn Raja's report.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, who said: 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from 'Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah used to give some members of the detachments he sent an additional share specifically for themselves, apart from the general army's division, and the fifth remained due in full.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi informed us: Hushaym informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, who used to sit with Abu Qatadah. He said: Abu Qatadah related the hadith.
Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Umar ibn Kathir, from Abu Muhammad, the freedman of Abu Qatadah, that Abu Qatadah related the hadith.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah informed us—the wording is Abu al-Tahir's—'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: I heard Malik ibn Anas say: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from 'Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, from Abu Muhammad, the freedman of Abu Qatadah, from Abu Qatadah, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah in the year of Hunayn. When we met the enemy, the Muslims were put to flight. I saw a polytheist standing over a Muslim. I circled around until I came behind him and struck him on the shoulder. He turned toward me and squeezed me so hard I felt the breath of death, then death overtook him and he released me. I caught up with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who asked what was happening with the people. I said: It is Allah's decree. Then the people returned, and the Messenger of Allah sat down and said: Whoever kills an enemy and has evidence for it is entitled to that person's belongings. I stood and said: Who will testify for me? Then I sat down. He said the same again, and I stood and asked who would testify for me, then sat down. He said it a third time. The Messenger of Allah asked: What is the matter, Abu Qatadah? I told him the story. A man among the people said: He is telling the truth, Messenger of Allah. The belongings of that slain man are with me, so give him what is due to him. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: No, by Allah! He will not take them from a little Qurayshi and leave a lion among Allah's lions who fights for Allah and His Messenger. The Messenger of Allah said: He is right; give them to him. The man gave them to me. I sold the armor and bought an orchard in Banu Salimah; it was the first property I established for myself in Islam. Al-Layth's report says Abu Bakr said: Certainly not! He will not give it to a little Qurayshi and leave a lion among Allah's lions. Al-Layth's report also says: It was the first property I established.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi informed us: Yusuf ibn al-Majishun informed us, from Salih ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: While I stood in the ranks on the day of Badr, I looked to my right and left and found myself between two young Ansari boys. I wished I were between men stronger than them. One nudged me and said: Uncle, do you know Abu Jahl? I said: Yes. What do you need him for, nephew? He said: I have been told he insults the Messenger of Allah. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if I see him, I will not part from his shadow until the one of us whose death is nearer dies. I was amazed at that. The other nudged me and said the same. Soon I saw Abu Jahl moving among the people. I said: Do you not see? That is the man you asked about. They rushed at him and struck him with their swords until they killed him. Then they went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. He asked: Which of you killed him? Each said: I did. He asked: Did you wipe your swords? They said no. He looked at the two swords and said: Both of you killed him. He awarded his belongings to Mu'adh ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh. The two men were Mu'adh ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Mu'adh ibn 'Afra'.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh informed us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from his father, from 'Awf ibn Malik, who said: A man from Himyar killed an enemy and wanted his belongings, but Khalid ibn al-Walid, who was in charge of them, withheld them. 'Awf ibn Malik went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. He said to Khalid: What prevented you from giving him the man's belongings? Khalid said: I thought they were a great deal, Messenger of Allah. He said: Give them to him. Khalid passed 'Awf and tugged his cloak, then asked whether he had fulfilled what he had mentioned from the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah heard him and became angry. He said: Do not give it to him, Khalid! Do not give it to him, Khalid! Will you leave my commanders alone? Your example and theirs is like that of a man entrusted with camels or sheep who tends them, then waits for their watering time and brings them to a pool. They drink the clear water and leave the turbid water. The clear water is for you, and the turbid is for them.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Safwan ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: I went with those who set out with Zayd ibn Harithah on the expedition of Mu'tah, and a reinforcement from Yemen accompanied me. He related the hadith from the Prophet in a similar way, except that 'Awf said: I asked Khalid, Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah awarded the slain man's belongings to the killer? He said: Yes, but I thought they were a great deal.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to me: my father, Salamah ibn al-Akwa', narrated to me: We fought Hawazin with the Messenger of Allah. While we were having a midday meal with him, a man came on a red camel, made it kneel, took a cord from its saddle strap, and tethered it. He went forward to eat with the people, looking around. Among us were weak men, short on mounts, and some were on foot. Suddenly he ran to his camel, untied it, made it kneel, mounted it, and drove it off at a run. A man followed him on a gray she-camel. Salamah said: I ran out and came beside the she-camel's hindquarters. Then I moved ahead to the camel's hindquarters, then farther until I caught its bridle and made it kneel. When the man put his knee on the ground, I drew my sword and struck his head, which fell away. I then brought the camel, leading it with its saddle and weapons. The Messenger of Allah and the people met me. He asked: Who killed the man? They said: Ibn al-Akwa'. He said: All of the man's belongings are his.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to me: my father said: We fought Fazara, with Abu Bakr in command; the Messenger of Allah had appointed him over us. When we were about an hour from the water, Abu Bakr ordered us to camp. Then he launched a raid and reached the water. He killed those he killed there and took captives. I saw a group of people, including children, and feared they would reach the mountain before me. I shot an arrow between them and the mountain. When they saw it, they stopped. I came and drove them along. Among them was a woman from Banu Fazara wearing a leather covering—al-Qish' means a leather mat—with a daughter of hers who was among the most beautiful of the Arabs. I drove them until I brought them to Abu Bakr, who gave me the daughter as an additional share. We arrived in Madinah, and I had not even uncovered her garment. The Messenger of Allah met me in the market and said: Salamah, give me the woman. I said: Messenger of Allah, by Allah, she has captivated me, and I have not uncovered her garment. The next day the Messenger of Allah met me in the market again and said: Salamah, may your father be sacrificed for you, give me the woman for Allah's sake. I said: She is yours, Messenger of Allah. By Allah, I have not uncovered her garment. The Messenger of Allah sent her to the people of Makkah and ransomed with her some Muslims who had been captured there.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. Among those reports he said: Any town you enter and settle in, your share is there. Any town that disobeys Allah and His Messenger, one fifth of its spoils belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and the rest is yours.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, Muhammad ibn 'Abbad, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. The wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah's. Ishaq said: Sufyan informed us; the others said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws, from 'Umar, who said: The property of Banu al-Nadir was among what Allah granted His Messenger without the Muslims having driven horses or camels against it. It belonged exclusively to the Prophet. He used to provide his family with a year's maintenance, and whatever remained he set aside for horses and weapons as preparation in Allah's cause.
Yahya ibn Yahya said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, with this chain.
